title: Fresh Thai Spring Rolls
description: Fresh Thai Spring Rolls are light, refreshing, and packed with crisp vegetables, fresh herbs, rice vermicelli, and your choice of shrimp, chicken, or tofu. Wrapped in delicate rice paper and served with a rich peanut dipping sauce or sweet chili sauce, they are a perfect appetizer or light meal.

ingredients.title: For the Rolls
items: Rice paper wrappers (22 cm diameter) – 8 sheets
Medium shrimp – 8, cooked, peeled, sliced in half lengthwise (or use tofu/chicken)
Thinly sliced cucumber (julienned, seeds removed) – 1 cup

ingredients.title: Protein Alternatives
items: Crispy or marinated tofu – pan-fried or baked

ingredients.title: Peanut Dipping Sauce (Thai-style)
items: Brown sugar or palm sugar – 1 tbsp
Red curry paste or Sriracha – 1 tsp (optional, for heat)

ingredients.title: Sweet Chili Sauce Alternative
items: Or mix: 1/4 cup sweet chili sauce + 1 tsp lime juice + 1/2 tsp fish sauce for balance

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Noodles
steps: Cook rice vermicelli noodles per package instructions (typically 3–4 minutes in boiling water).
Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Prep Fillings
steps: Wash, peel, and julienne all vegetables.
Arrange fresh herbs for quick access.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Soften Rice Paper
steps: Fill a wide shallow bowl or pan with warm water.
Dip one rice paper sheet in the water for 4–6 seconds, until just pliable (not too soft—it will continue softening as you roll).
Lay it flat on a damp clean cutting board or kitchen towel.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Fill and Roll
steps: Place a few mint, basil, and cilantro leaves in the center.
Layer a small bundle of noodles, carrots, cucumbers, cabbage, and sprouts.
Top with 2–3 shrimp halves (pink side down for visual appeal).
Fold in the sides, then roll tightly from the bottom like a burrito.
Tip: Do not overfill! Tightly packed but not bursting is key.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Repeat
steps: Continue with remaining wrappers and filling.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve chilled or at room temperature with peanut or chili dipping sauce.
Garnish with extra herbs, crushed peanuts, or a lime wedge on the side.

chefTips: Drink: Thai iced tea, lemongrass iced green tea, or a crisp white wine like Sauvignon Blanc.
Side: Pair with Tom Yum soup or Papaya Salad (Som Tum) for a full Thai meal.
